label: copy-phase input v (not the first copied token)
explanation: Token detector for v fed back as input during the copy phase. Never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>; essentially 100% of activations have in_tok == v (13 tiny exceptions on u). Inside the copy phase it is almost always silent when v is the first copied input (recall_idx 1, i.e. orig(0) == v): rate 0.7% there vs about 3% of steps at recall_idx >= 2, and those activations sit in the lowest quartile. Magnitude grows with how far into the copy the v appears: the top activations are v near the end of long sequences (L 8-9), and early-position v gives activations of 0.1-0.3 of max. Adding recall_idx >= 2 takes dev F1 from 0.87 to 0.92 (precision 0.77 to 0.90) and keeps 98% of the activation mass.

issues: Minor misstatement: the 0.7% vs about 3% rates are rates over all copy steps at each recall_idx, not over v inputs. Counting only copy-phase v inputs, the feature fires on about 22% of first-copied v (recall_idx==1: precision 0.219, 16980 predicted). At recall_idx==2 it fires on about 82%, and at recall_idx>=3 on about 92%. So 'almost always silent' on the first copied v overstates it: it is mostly silent and weak, holding only 1.9% of activation mass.

The remaining false positives (7366 on test) are a graded effect, not a separate class. Precision drops at early steps and short sequences: t<=8 gives 0.75 and L<=5 gives 0.78, against 0.94 at t>=10 or L>=8. This fits the stated 'magnitude grows the later v appears'. Splitting on correct, prev_tok type, next_out or in_count turned up no clean exception class.

Alternatives did not beat the original in a meaningful way. On dev, (phase==2)&v&((recall_idx>=2)|(L>=8)) gives F1 0.926 against 0.923. The t>=K thresholds and adding t>=7 are worse (F1 0.87 to 0.915).

The other claims check out. The feature never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>. 70588 of the 70601 dev activations are on v, plus 12 on u and 1 on j. The test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.901, R 0.947, F1 0.924, mass 0.981).
